html:
The room in Blender

room.blend (Git LFS) is the source of the 3D room on /. Four scripts rebuild, bake and export it. They run headless with Blender 5.2 LTS, Cycles on the CPU.

build_room.py ──► room.blend ──► bake.py ──► .cache/bake/*.png|exr ──► export.py ──► public/room/
 Henry's layout     (scene)       room atlases (env,                   (display-ready)   room.glb (KTX2 + meshopt)
 + room, lights     desk, props) without the view;                                    window_{sf,delhi}_{day,night}.ktx2
 + room_dressing.py               the view's halves alone,                            poster.avif, poster.jpg
 + window_view.py                 by day and by night                                 renders/room_*.png, window_view.png

Re-bake

blender -b blender/room.blend -P blender/scripts/bake.py

room.blend reads its downloaded textures, models and font from blender/.cache/ (git-ignored), so on a fresh clone run the rebuild below once before baking. Bakes the three room atlases (env, desk, props; 4096² each) at 512 samples, then each half of the window view (window_sf, window_delhi; 1024² each) by day and by night, on 24 threads, and saves the bake UVs into room.blend. The room atlases bake without the view (a camera-invisible card behind the window, lit by Poly Haven's dusk HDRI, lights the room); the view bakes alone with its own sun, sky and night lights. For a quick look, bake small: -- --scale 0.25 --samples 32, one atlas: -- --atlas desk, or the view only: -- --atlas window_sf,window_delhi.

Re-export

blender -b blender/room.blend -P blender/scripts/export.py

Renders the stills, writes the view's four KTX2 files (ETC1S with mipmaps, ktx create), exports the glb, then runs gltf-transform 4.5.1 (via npx): dedup, prune (empties and attributes kept), KTX2 ETC1S atlases, meshopt geometry. The atlases ship resampled from their 4096² bakes (EXPORT_SIZES: desk 3584, props 2944, env 2560), which keeps the glb inside 4.3 MB. It then points each view half's material at its day texture by URI. It fails if room.glb is over 4.3 MB, the two day textures are over 400 KB together, or a node from the contract below is missing. Needs Node (npx), ktx from KTX-Software 4.x and ffmpeg with libaom on PATH. -- --no-stills exports only the glb and textures; -- --only room_idle,window_view renders some stills.

Stills: renders/room_{idle,desk,shelf,window,projector,photos}.png, renders/window_view.png (the cam_window framing, plain; src/os/assets/wallpaper/build.mjs turns it into the SaahilOS wallpaper with its film look) and public/room/poster.{avif,jpg} (the cam_idle view). They show San Francisco at dusk and Delhi by day, the four Letterboxd favourites from public/room/posters/ and the photographs the photography collection puts on the wall (src/assets/photography/). In the glb those pictures are runtime textures, so re-export the stills when the favourites or the wall's photographs change.

Rebuild from scratch

blender -b --factory-startup -P blender/scripts/build_room.py

Downloads Henry Heffernan's three models (pinned commit, checked by sha256), the CC0 textures, HDRI and models from Poly Haven and ambientCG, and Newsreader (pinned commit, sha256) into blender/.cache/, then builds the scene and overwrites room.blend. Props are appended from blender/props/<name>.blend (root collection named after the prop; rebuild them with python3 blender/scripts/props_build.py --render). Re-bake after a rebuild.

window_view.py also renders the view alone for quick work on it: blender -b --factory-startup -P blender/scripts/window_view.py -- <out_dir> day cam_window.

What the glb holds

Node What
env_* walls, floor, window, curtains, sill, radiator, shelf, fixtures, rug, side table, sideboard, photo lamp
desk_* desk, chair, computer, CRT, keyboard, mouse, cables, lamp, papers, mug, notebook, sticky notes, headphones; photo_album
props_* props from blender/props/ and the dressing (books, records, plants, frames, lantern, jacket …)
crt_glow, lamp_bulb, lava_lamp_glass, oven_glow, nas_led_0..3 runtime meshes, each with its own unlit material (nas_led is shared by the four LEDs) so the site can tint, flicker or replace them
window_view_sf, window_view_delhi the view's halves (the seam is x = 1.33 m, behind the window's central bar); material = that half's day texture by URI; extras texture_day, texture_night
poster_art_0..3 the poster pictures, slot 0 leftmost seen from the room; TEXCOORD_0 = 0–1 over the 2:3 picture for the art; material poster_art_<slot> holds the baked light on the picture on TEXCOORD_1
photo_print_0..4 the photo wall's pictures, same scheme; extras photo_slot, aspect, width_m, height_m (slots 0–2 are 1:1, 4:3, 16:9 for the three prints marked for the wall; 3 is 3:2, 4 is 4:5)
poster_plaque "Four favourites — from Letterboxd", engraved and baked
lava_lamp, espresso_machine, countertop_oven, ceiling_fan, mango_fruit baked bodies of the round-two props
ceiling_fan_blades, projector_dial pivots (empties at the hub / dial axis) holding <name>_mesh; turn them about their local +Y
hit_* invisible click boxes (material proxy): the T3 set plus hit_window, hit_projector_screen, hit_lava_lamp, hit_fan, hit_espresso, hit_oven, hit_plaque, hit_photo_wall, hit_album, hit_projector_dial; hit_poster_<id> keep their T3 names and carry extras poster_slot
monitor_screen centre of the CRT glass; local +Z out of the glass; extras width_m, height_m
projector_lens, projector_screen_center beam origin (local −Z along the beam) and its target
lava_lamp_light, espresso_steam the lamp's light centre; the steam's start at the portafilter spouts
album_open_anchor where the opened album floats, 0.55 m in front of cam_desk, local +Z toward the camera; extras width_m, height_m
cam_loading, cam_idle, cam_desk, cam_monitor, cam_shelf, cam_projector, cam_window, cam_photos camera framings, each with a <name>_target look-at empty; extras fov_deg (vertical)

Units are metres, +Y up. Every material is KHR_materials_unlit with the baked light as its base colour, already tone-mapped (AgX, exposure 2.15, the same as the stills), so the site shows it with no tone mapping and sRGB output. The atlas materials are room_env, room_desk and room_props; only room_props_leaves (the mango leaves, same texture as room_props) is double-sided, because thin closed shells z-fight through a double-sided material.

For the art meshes the light on the picture is baked on white paper, so the site can draw art × light: put the runtime art in map (TEXCOORD_0), move the baked texture to lightMap (GLTFLoader already gives it channel 1) and set lightMapIntensity to π. For the view, blend window_<half>_day.ktx2 and window_<half>_night.ktx2 by that city's local time; to soften the seam, blend by world x across the seam instead of per mesh (both halves' textures match at the seam in each state).

Lights

Each light has a source in the room: the desk lamp (tungsten, about 2700 K), the projector (cool #9DB4C0 spot from projector_lens, plus the lit picture on the screen), the CRT glass, dusk through the window (an emissive card behind the window and a soft area light), the brass picture light over the posters, the strip light under the top shelf and the fairy lights along it, the lava lamp's glow on the posters and plaque, the oven's elements, the photo wall's picture lamp, a red darkroom safelight, and a paper lantern in the reading corner. A camera-invisible ceiling and front and right walls bounce light like a closed room; they are never baked or exported. The view has its own lights (sun and sky by day; moon, floodlights on the monuments and the bridge, city glow by night) in window_lights, switched on only while its halves bake.

Budget

The glb holds about 100k vertices: the props' prop files keep their full detail, and build_room.py decimates the densest ones for the room only (DECIMATE). The view keeps only faces some framing, or a glide between two framings, can see through the window. Credits for every downloaded model, texture, HDRI and font are in ASSETS.md.
